desc: Ideate and select the right-endpoint sweep approach.
Normalize every conflicting pair to (x,y) with x < y and bucket pairs by y.
Sweep r=1..n, processing all pairs with the same y as one batch before evaluating that endpoint.
Maintain the largest active x (top1), its active count, its unique owner pair id, and the second-largest distinct active x (top2).
Accumulate the baseline valid-subarray count and per-pair gains incrementally: baseline += r - top1; if top1 is unique, gain[owner] += top1 - top2.
Return baseline + max gain, treating missing gains as 0 so exactly one pair is always removed.
Validate with examples and edge cases: single pair, duplicate pairs, same smaller endpoint, dominated pairs, and all pairs redundant.
